panels.title: No Route
panels.description: Requests that hit the listener and matched no HTTPRoute — a missing or misspelled hostname.

panels.title: Requests by Response Class
panels.description: Response classes are ordered state, not identity — 5xx is painted critical and 4xx warning so a bad deploy is visible without reading the legend.

panels.title: Upstream p99 by Route
panels.description: Time the backend took, excluding the gateway's own overhead.

panels.title: Healthy Backends
panels.description: Endpoints Envoy currently considers healthy per route. Zero means the service is up but nothing is behind it.

panels.title: Blocking Enabled
panels.description: Blocking can be paused at runtime through blocky's API. This is the panel that explains a sudden drop in the blocked ratio.

panels.title: Denylist Entries
panels.description: Domains currently blocked. A collapse to zero means a list refresh failed.

panels.title: Failed Downloads (24h)
panels.description: A denylist source blocky could not fetch. The old list stays loaded, so this fails quietly.

panels.title: Blocky Responses by Type
panels.description: BLOCKED / CACHED / RESOLVED / SPECIAL. The shape of this stack is the single best read on whether blocky is doing its job.

panels.title: Queries by Client
panels.description: Which device on the LAN is actually asking. 25 clients are tracked; this shows the busiest ten.

panels.title: Upstream Resolvers
panels.description: Which upstream answered. `reason` carries the resolver address, so an upstream going dark shows up as its series flatlining.

panels.title: Blocky Query Types
panels.description: A/AAAA/HTTPS/PTR and friends.

panels.title: CoreDNS Request Rate
panels.description: Cluster-internal resolver, not the LAN one.

panels.title: CoreDNS Responses by Rcode
panels.description: Sustained NXDOMAIN usually means something is resolving a name that no longer exists.

panels.title: Layer 2 Announcements
panels.description: A burst here means a service IP moved between nodes.

panels.title: Internet
panels.description: The probe that separates 'my cluster broke' from 'my ISP broke'.

panels.title: Soonest TLS Expiry
panels.description: Measured from the served certificate chain, not from cert-manager's own bookkeeping — this is what a browser would actually see.

panels.title: Endpoint Status
panels.description: Probed from inside the cluster, so a tale.me target exercises DNS, the gateway, its certificate and the backend — but the packet may never leave the building.

panels.title: Unmanaged Pods
panels.description: Pods Cilium never took ownership of — they have no policy applied.

panels.title: Policy Drops by Workload

defaults.noValue: No flows denied in this range

panels.description: Denials run about eight a day here, so this counts over the selected range rather than rating over 5m. Empty means nothing was denied in the window, which is the answer you want.

panels.title: BPF Map Pressure
panels.description: Fraction of a BPF map's capacity in use. Approaching 1 means Cilium is about to start refusing to program the datapath.
